title: Exposure Thermostat Framework (working draft)
content:
Purpose:
- Provide a lightweight, cross-functional operating metaphor for progressive exposure of LLM features (think of exposure as a thermostat, not a faucet).
- Help product, SRE/Observability, applied-ML, and CS teams agree on how to warm up, hold steady, and cool down traffic safely.

Why the thermostat metaphor?
- Thermostat = target-driven, continuous monitoring with small-actuation corrections.
- Avoids binary on/off thinking (big-bang deploys) and complements staged-slices/canaries by focusing on steady-state control loops.

High level summary (one-liner):
- Incremental exposure guided by target signals (quality + safety + cost + latency) with a named steward, automated guardrails, and a human-in-loop escalation ladder.

Guiding principles
- SLO-first: exposure only increases if primary SLOs (latency, correctness for prompt set, safety thresholds) are within tolerance for X minutes.
- Conservative compounding: increase exposure in small steps (e.g., +2–5% user weight or +5 qps) and observe for multiple signal windows.
- Multi-signal consensus: require at least 3 of 4 signal groups (latency, quality, safety, infra) to be green before next step.
- Fast revertability: any automated increase must have an easy way to instantly revert (traffic switch, route override).
- Cost-aware gating: if per-token/$ impact exceeds guard, revert to cheaper variant automatically.
- Clear ownership: steward owns the thermostat schedule and communication during warm-up.

Roles and responsibilities
- Steward (activation steward): orchestrates the warm-up, owns the hypothesis, primary contact for alerts.
- Observability owner: ensures dashboards, real-time slices, and alert thresholds are configured ahead of exposure.
- Model owner / Applied ML: owns prompt set and quality evaluation harness, identifies known failure modes.
- SRE/Infra: manages capacity ladders (bursting, spillover targets) and enacts immediate emergency rollback if system risk.
- CS / Ops: prepares comms for customers in case of degraded behavior (pre-approved templates).

Thermostat configuration (suggested defaults)
- Initial exposure: 1% traffic, or a fixed small synthetic-traffic baseline.
- Step increment: +3% traffic (or +10 concurrent sessions), configurable per feature.
- Hold window: 30 minutes min for critical signals, 2 hours for behavioral metrics (quality/safety).
- Stability requirement: 3 consecutive hold windows green to double step size OR continue steady increments.
- Max exposure before manual review: 40% (unless enterprise agreement allows higher).

Signals (clusters) and example metrics
- Latency (infra): p95 request latency, per-model queue depth, GPU saturation, error rate (5xx).
- Quality (eval-driven): prompt-set acceptance rate, token-level perplexity shifts, task-specific pass/fail ratio, human eval snippets sampled.
- Safety (content): classifier triggers per 1k requests, escalation events, false-positive/false-negative drift.
- Cost: tokens per request, per-token unit cost, budget burn rate vs projection.
- User impact: NPS/CS complaints, front-end dropped sessions, observed churn signals (if available).

Decision logic (simplified)
- Green = all critical infra metrics AND majority of quality/safety metrics within thresholds for hold window.
- Yellow = one critical metric close to threshold or 2 non-critical metrics degraded. Pause increases, notify steward, run targeted synthetic tests.
- Red = any critical infra alert (p95 > threshold, GPU OOM, high error rate) OR safety classifier spike beyond emergency threshold. Immediate rollback to last-known-good exposure.

Automations and runbooks to build
- Auto-bump script: increments traffic by configured step after hold window passes and central CI checks pass. Includes a canary tag for tracing.
- Auto-freeze: if cost or safety delta > configured % within window, freeze thermostat and page steward.
- Emergency rollback: a single click/command to switch routing to baseline model and set thermostat to 0% exposure.
- Synthetic probes: pre-built prompt basket routed at each step to detect behavioral regression quickly.

Steward checklist (pre-start)
- Confirm steward identity and on-call overlap.
- Finalize thermostat config (initial exposure, step size, hold windows, max exposure).
- Confirm metrics dashboards and slices (by georegion, customer tier, route).
- Confirm linked artifacts (PRs, model build id, tag, migration notes).
- Create comms plan with CS and Ops (template messages ready).
- Schedule a 1-hr watch window with on-call coverage for first 2 steps.

Steward checklist (during warm-up)
- Note time of each step increase and attach run id to PagerDuty incident (if any).
- Manually inspect sampled outputs for quality drift at each step.
- Validate synthetic probe results (pass/fail, exact diffs).
- Watch for non-linear signals (e.g., small latency increase but big classifier spike).

Rollback matrix (example)
- Trigger: p95 latency > 1.5x baseline for 15 minutes => action: immediate rollback, page infra lead.
- Trigger: safety classifier > 20x historical baseline in small window => rollback and full sample audit.
- Trigger: quality acceptance rate drops > 10% vs baseline => pause and run expanded human review.
- Trigger: cost burn > projected +30% => throttle exposure and notify finance.

Traffic shaping patterns to consider
- Micro-sampling: seed a tiny percentage of users for long-lived sessions to uncover session-level drift.
- Route-level gating: only send low-risk routes (e.g., info retrieval) first, gate high-risk routes (payments, identity) later.
- Customer-tier windows: increase exposure for internal/beta customers faster than public traffic.
- Time-of-day scheduling: avoid large increases during peak traffic or manual maintenance windows.

Observability cookbook (quick list)
- Pre-made slice dashboards: by route, model, prompt family, user-cohort, region.
- Synthetic probe runner: run every 5 minutes during warm-up, record diffs to baseline.
- Sampling recorder: capture 1 in N real outputs at each step, auto-attach to run id.
- Alerting thresholds: conservative defaults checked into repo; steward can opt-in to stricter values.

Examples (scenarios)
- Scenario A: reranker model update. Start 1% -> +3% every 30m. Synthetic rerank tests run; quality green for 4 windows => reach 13% then manual review before 40%.
- Scenario B: new streaming completion mode (latency sensitive). Start 0.5% with tighter latency windows (15m). Any p95 shift > 10% halts increase.
- Scenario C: enterprise private deployment. Thermostat is controlled by customer policy; default server-side limits enforce hard caps.

Communication templates (to copy/paste)
- Pre-activation: "Activating feature X at 1% traffic starting 2025-10-05 09:00 PT. Steward: Avery Chen. Monitoring dashboard: <link>. Expecting 3–6 hour staged warm-up. Will send updates at each step"
- Emergency: "Rollback executed for feature X at 2025-10-05 11:42 PT due to p95 latency spike. Traffic reverted to baseline. Investigating. Pager: @oncall-infra."

Open questions / TODOs
- How do we standardize the "majority of signal clusters" rule numerically? (need exact quorum algorithm).
- Should we build a library of graduated synthetic probe baskets per product vertical? (yes, prioritize search/rerank first).
- Integrate cost forecast estimation into thermostat auto-decision engine (requires finance input).
- UX: add an exposure timeline visualization to Console (show step times, state, signals).

Appendix: quick references and links
- CONFLUENCE-1234: rollout guardrails canonical page
- JIRA-RF-987: thermostat automation epic
- PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/thermostat-runner (WIP)

Notes to self: keep this intentionally lightweight and modular. The aim is to reduce cognitive load on cross-functional teams while giving a clear control loop. Next steps: run a tabletop with SRE + Applied ML + Product next week, then prototype a one-click freeze/rollback in Console.

-- end of draft --
